rationale: The slow-store probe ran (CheckRun 394ae390a0164b5dbda779132c28478d, exit 0) and returned a second zero - 768 deliveries, 4605 term samples, no falls, the term climbing monotonically to 2306 in memory and in the store - and thinking about why is worth more than the count. Two structural reasons emerge, and both narrow the hazard's preconditions rather than refuting it. First, the deliveries that create the off-thread write are the same events that refresh the follower's last contact, so a stream of them keeps the node from ever starting the election it would need to collide with; a campaign needs silence, and a heartbeat ends the silence. Second, and sharper: with a uniform store latency both writers sleep the same amount, so the write that starts later - the heartbeat's, since it arrives after the campaign began - finishes later and lands last, which means the higher term wins and no fall can occur. The fall requires the opposite ordering, the main loop's write being applied after the off-thread one, which the gate produced by holding that write open while the heartbeat's write completed. So what the hazard needs is not merely overlap but an asymmetry in when the two writes take effect, which is why neither denser delivery nor a uniformly slower store raises the rate. I record the observation, answer the open question with that conditional account, and state the resulting precondition plainly instead of leaving the timing story as an unexplained narrow window.

knowledge.statement: On one real single-node Raft instance over a store whose write of the current-term key sleeps 3 ms before applying, 768 fast-path deliveries all succeeded and 4605 term samples were taken among them with no sample below the highest term already adopted; the term ended at 2306 in memory and in the stable store with the node in Follower state. A uniform slow term write did not produce the regression in this schedule.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot 09193ea9b7ee4df99810e6eee7058028; single-voter node, in-memory transport wrapped for the heartbeat fast path, store that sleeps on the current-term write only, heartbeats delivered continuously three terms above the node's current term with six samples after each; no hold-open hook of any kind.

interpretations.rationale: The open question was whether the rate rises when the window is wide rather than a couple of instructions, and this probe answers no for the configuration it tests, but the reason is the valuable part. With the current-term write sleeping three milliseconds, the window is as wide as the probe can make it without a hook, deliveries overlap it constantly, 4605 samples were taken, and still no fall appeared. Two structural facts explain why. The first is that a heartbeat refreshes the follower's last contact, so the deliveries that would collide with an election also keep it from ever starting: an election needs the absence of heartbeats, and the probe supplied no absence. The second is decisive for the ordering: with a uniform latency both writers sleep for the same time, so the heartbeat's write, which begins after the election's, completes after it and is applied last, which leaves the higher term in place - the opposite of a fall. The regression therefore does not merely need the two writes to overlap; it needs the main loop's write to take effect after the off-thread one, which is what the gate arranged by holding that write open until the heartbeat's write had completed. That is a precondition on scheduling asymmetry rather than on window width, and it explains both zeros without weakening the witnessed cases: a fast persistent path for heartbeats against a delayed, contended path for the election's own write is the shape that produces the ordering, and it is exactly the shape a fast heartbeat handler next to a slow main-thread persist can create. I answer the gap with this condition and keep the defect claim where it belongs, on the mechanism and the three receipts that show it, rather than on either probe's zero, which I read as a bound on how easily the ordering arises and not as evidence against it.

answers.2aa9e9b7af1840e9b90e8ceced03c800-gap-6: Conditional and, in this configuration, no. Denser delivery does not help because every heartbeat refreshes the follower's last contact and so postpones or prevents the election it would have to collide with, and a uniformly slower store does not help either: with equal write latencies the write that starts later - the heartbeat's - finishes later and is applied last, leaving the higher term in place, so overlap alone produces no fall. The regression needs the main loop's write to take effect after the off-thread one, which is an asymmetry in scheduling rather than a wide window; the gate achieved it by holding that write open, and a fast heartbeat write against a delayed contended election write is the shape that would achieve it naturally.

counterevidence: Two zeros in the uninstrumented probes show the ordering is not easy to reach under equal treatment of the two writers; they bound the rate and do not refute the mechanism, which the three earlier receipts establish.
The asymmetry argument is source-based: it follows from which write starts later under equal latency, and the probes did not construct the contended-persist configuration that would test it.
Both probes still deliver through the wrapper transport that mirrors the network transport rather than the network transport itself, and both are single-voter.
The node never started an election during the slow-store probe, so that run does not measure the collision even at the write ordering; it measures that continuous delivery suppresses the campaign.
limitations: This is a conditional answer about what the probes could reach, not a measurement of a real deployment's write scheduling; the contention shape that would produce the required ordering was not constructed here.
Eight seconds and 768 deliveries with one simulated latency, one cluster shape: the negative bounds the rate for this configuration.
The gate receipts remain the only place where the ordering is established, and they establish it by construction rather than by observing it arise on its own.
interpretations.joint_history: Same investigation and same setup as the natural-timing probe, with one change: the store sleeps before applying the current-term write, so the interval the off-thread write must land in is as wide as the simulated durable latency. The earlier receipts establish that the interleaving is possible, reproducible and attributable to the off-thread write, with the gate creating the ordering deliberately; these two probes ask what happens without any hook.
